The keyword-answer strategy

Open-ended questions scare most students. We coach them with the keywords MOE markers look for — and the questions get harder, gradually, as the student gets stronger. Same concept, three difficulties:

Easy · keywords given

Why does sweating cool you down?

Use these keywords in your answer:

sweatevaporatesheatbodycooler
✓ Sweat evaporates and takes heat from the body, making it feel cooler.
Medium · pick the right keywords

Why does sweating cool you down?

Choose the keywords that apply:

evaporatesmeltsheatcoolerwarmercondenses
✓ Student must reject melts, warmer, condenses and write the full explanation using the correct ones.
Hard · no keywords

Why does sweating cool you down?

Write a full answer in your own words.

✓ Free response. Our marker spots the required concepts (evaporation, heat loss, cooling) and gives partial credit for each — same way MOE markers do.
How it works: the system tracks each student's accuracy on a concept. Get it right twice in a row at easy, it ramps to medium. Two more wins, and it removes the keywords entirely. Get one wrong, it gently steps back down. Students build the answer-writing muscle without getting demoralised — they always have a path forward.

Username ≥2 chars. Password ≥4 chars (required — students sign in with it). Level controls which topics are shown by default. Group is optional — use it to tag students by class (e.g. "Mon-3pm").

📥 Bulk upload (whole class)

Paste one account per line in CSV format: username,password,expiry_date,level,group
Expiry: YYYY-MM-DD. Level: P3/P4/P5/P6. Group: any short label (e.g. Mon-3pm). Username and password are required (password ≥4 chars); expiry, level and group can be left blank.
Example:
ayden,Welcome2026,2027-05-31,P5,Mon-3pm
marcus,Welcome2026,2027-05-31,P5,Mon-3pm
chloe,Welcome2026,2027-05-31,P6,Sat-10am

Existing usernames will be skipped.
